consumer_contexts: menu, inventory, tutorial, and dialogue text in games shipped to several regions
training, industrial, and accessibility XR applications that must switch language at runtime
common_kernel: stable message identity separate from translated content
locale identity with explicit, reported fallback
message formatting with plural and select branches
per-locale content validation with stable diagnostic codes
configurable_variation: default locale, fallback preferences, declared plural language set, and adapter-side table storage
consumer-owned strings, tone, fonts, layout, and translation workflow
excluded_project_specific: one product's string tables, glossary, voice, and brand names
one project's asset layout, loading strategy, UI, and font choices
rationale: Localization is a recurring cross-project need whose kernel (identity, fallback, formatting, validation) is fixed by public standards, while every product keeps its own content, fonts, and pipeline outside the shared Core.
non_claims: Admission does not claim CLDR completeness, script rendering, right-to-left layout, or Unity Localization runtime behavior; this draft becomes a decision only when a maintainer copies it into docs/foundry/admissions/ after confirming the sources.
